palette.notes: None of the 3 clips show the game (occult book drawings, 80s fantasy paintings), so no palette was seen. Wiki gives no palette detail.

lighting: Not seen in frames; the wiki does not describe lighting. Its one visual award (IndieCade 2011 Visuals) is the only signal.
silhouette: Per sources.yaml: minimal, tall-pixel characters. Cast is a few iconic figures (the Scythian warrior, Girl the shepherd, Logfella and his dog Dogfella, an antlered giant), each one simple shape (wiki).

motion.timing: No frame timings measured and no game frames seen. Wiki: actions are slow and deliberate (tap to walk, hold the hero to sing, tilt the device to draw the sword).

texture: Not seen. Reviewers compare its surface to a ~1995 point-and-click adventure (wiki).
camera: Wiki: mobile versions use device orientation during play; tilting the device 90 degrees switches the hero into sword-drawn combat. The frame itself changes shape with the mode.
sound: Jim Guthrie score is part of the play: holding the hero starts a song, boss attacks follow the music, a rock-concert scene (wiki).

acting.acts: Wiki: the hero acts through few, ritual gestures (sleep at a hearth to switch to the dream world, sing to solve puzzles, raise the sword). Each gesture is a mode change, not a busy loop.
acting.exits: Leaving is by sleeping: the hero goes to a dream world and returns (wiki).

techniques: few iconic characters, each one simple tall shape
one held gesture per action (hold to sing, tilt to draw sword)
orientation change as a mode switch: wide for walking, tall for combat
music drives the action: attacks timed to the song
sleep/dream world as a clean way to leave and return
feel: few tall minimal figures + one ritual gesture per beat + music-led timing = calm, mythic, cinematic (from text only)
for_fred: Give Fred one ritual gesture that means 'mode change' (e.g. a slow 3-frame pose before a gag) and use it only at turning points; in a vertical reel let a beat land on the music, not on every word. Note: written from the wiki only, no game frames were usable.
